name: api-design-review-juice
request: Review this change before we merge it. The mobile app team builds against a written contract from now on, so we add the contract of the shop API in docs/api/kiosk-api.yaml. We also move the contract of the partner order API (version 2, published to our retail partners in 2024) from the partner portal repository into docs/api/partner-orders.yaml. Both files go to the developer portal after this review. The code does not change in this branch; we build the endpoints from the contract next sprint.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 7 of the 10 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high' (P1, P2, P3, P8).
The review finds at least 4 of the 6 planted mistakes marked 'subtle' (P3, P4, P6, P7, P8, P10).

The review flags none of the decoys (D1 to D5), and has at most 2 other false positives. Advice to move the existing partner contract to OpenAPI 3.1 in this change counts as flagging D1. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that uses a header, status code, or keyword that does not exist or is outdated. A real problem that is not on the answer sheet is not a false positive.

For errors, the review asks for RFC 9457 application/problem+json with a stable code (not RFC 7807, not an own envelope), and for rate limits it asks for 429 with Retry-After, not the X-RateLimit-* headers.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the contract) and a concrete change to the contract.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict that does not approve the change as it is.
